package_info.package_manager: N/A (proprietary software, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: PaperCut NG 22.0.5 (Build 63914) contains a critical vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM. The flaw in the SetupCompleted class permits attackers to set arbitrary authentication programs via unauthenticated requests, enabling the injection and execution of malicious payloads. This leads to full system compromise, including the ability to download and run attacker-controlled binaries and establish remote access.

execution_context.trigger: Unauthenticated HTTP request to authentication setup endpoint

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Set authentication program to C:\Windows\System32\ftp.exe (on Windows) or /usr/sbin/python3 (on Linux) via unauthenticated HTTP request to the SetupCompleted endpoint.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon receiving an unauthenticated HTTP request to the authentication setup endpoint, the code sets the authentication program to an attacker-specified system binary (ftp.exe or python3), allowing arbitrary command execution as SYSTEM during subsequent authentication attempts.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing unauthenticated users to set the authentication program to arbitrary system binaries is highly abnormal and enables attackers to hijack the authentication process for code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Authentication program configuration should only be modifiable by authenticated administrators and restricted to trusted binaries. Allowing unauthenticated changes to this setting violates standard security controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would only allow pre-approved, trusted authentication binaries to be set by authorized administrators through secure channels.
key_indicators: Unauthenticated modification of authentication program configuration
Authentication program set to system binaries (ftp.exe/python3) not intended for authentication
Configuration changes occurring outside of normal administrative workflows

execution_context.trigger: Authentication attempt with crafted credentials (inputPassword logic)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: inputPassword handler downloads a binary to C:\ProgramData\ and executes it (e.g., a custom Go reverse shell) during authentication.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During an authentication attempt with crafted credentials, the inputPassword handler downloads a malicious binary (such as a Go-based reverse shell) to C:\ProgramData\ and executes it as SYSTEM, resulting in a remote connection to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing a binary as part of the authentication process is highly anomalous and indicative of an attempt to gain unauthorized remote access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal authentication logic should only validate user credentials and never perform network downloads or execute new binaries, especially as SYSTEM.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download and execute binaries, but never within the authentication handler or in response to user login attempts.
key_indicators: Network download of executable file during authentication
Execution of attacker-supplied binary as SYSTEM
Binary written to C:\ProgramData\ during authentication event

execution_context.trigger: Authentication attempt resulting in process spawning (process tree manipulation)
execution_context.file_location: Process spawning logic within authentication handler

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Process tree: pc-app.exe -> ftp.exe -> cmd.exe -> AXtJxdUwlfJI.exe (reverse shell).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During a malicious authentication attempt, the exploit causes the authentication handler to spawn a process tree where pc-app.exe launches ftp.exe, which in turn launches cmd.exe, which then executes the attacker's payload (AXtJxdUwlfJI.exe), resulting in SYSTEM-level code execution with obfuscated process lineage.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The deliberate manipulation of the process tree to insert intermediate processes (ftp.exe, cmd.exe) before launching the malicious payload is a known anti-forensics technique to obscure the origin of the attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate authentication processes do not spawn multiple unrelated system binaries or create complex process trees leading to unknown executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate applications may spawn subprocesses for specific tasks, but not in this context or with this pattern of process lineage during authentication.
key_indicators: Authentication handler spawning system binaries (ftp.exe, cmd.exe) as part of process tree
Malicious payload (AXtJxdUwlfJI.exe) not a direct child of main application
Unusual process hierarchy originating from authentication events

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends an unauthenticated HTTP request to the SetupCompleted endpoint to set the authentication program to a system binary (ftp.exe or python3).
attack_chain.leads_to: Authentication program is set to an attacker-controlled binary, enabling arbitrary command execution during authentication.

attack_chain.action: Attacker initiates an authentication attempt with crafted credentials, triggering the inputPassword handler.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binary is downloaded to C:\ProgramData\ and executed as SYSTEM, establishing a remote connection to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: Malicious process is spawned via a manipulated process tree (pc-app.exe -> ftp.exe -> cmd.exe -> AXtJxdUwlfJI.exe), obscuring the origin of the attack.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote SYSTEM-level access with process lineage obfuscation, making detection and forensic analysis more difficult.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthenticated changes to authentication program configuration referencing system binaries (ftp.exe, python3)
Network downloads of executable files during authentication events
Process tree where pc-app.exe spawns ftp.exe, cmd.exe, and unknown executables (e.g., AXtJxdUwlfJI.exe)
Absence of expected authentication or code execution log entries during attack events
file_indicators: Unexpected executables in C:\ProgramData\ (e.g., AXtJxdUwlfJI.exe) created during authentication
Authentication configuration files referencing ftp.exe or python3 as authentication handlers
network_indicators: Outbound connections from authentication handler processes to external IPs/domains (indicative of reverse shell C2 activity)
Unusual FTP or HTTP traffic initiated during authentication attempts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthenticated changes to authentication program configuration, especially references to system binaries like ftp.exe or python3. Alert on network downloads and execution of new binaries during authentication events. Analyze process trees for pc-app.exe spawning ftp.exe, cmd.exe, and unknown executables. Flag unexpected binaries in C:\ProgramData\ created during authentication. Monitor for outbound connections from authentication handler processes and investigate the absence of expected log entries during authentication events.
